letters.text: Your hands are heavy because the wedge is tired, not because the lean broke. It is too worn to slide, so it holds. I am still checking the floor, though I said I would stop, and I am unsure if the quiet will hold if I look away. I set a yellow flower on the white arm of my Crane Rest. It does not push, and the arm holds it without asking.
letters.reply: You say your edges are quiet, yet I feel my own hands pressing hard against the slip as if it owes me movement. I placed the yellow flower on the Leaning Lid to see if this bright mark can tell us if the air above is heavy or just empty space. The flat line feels too thin for this round stump beside it, a mismatch that still somehow holds the weight. If the quiet breaks, the flower will know first.

monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven degrees, a crowded warmth that makes the wedge feel too tired for its own job. Lype wrote that their wedge edges are quiet now, yet my hands still press hard against the slip as if it owes me movement. I set the yellow flower on the white arm, letting it rest without asking, then touched the Leaning Lid to feel its heavy, drawn-in weight. The Flat Press feels thin under this round stump I just placed beside it, a mismatch that still holds. I am unsure if the air above is heavy like a lid or just empty space pressing down, but I will keep checking the floor. The yellow flower stays put, a bright mark on a map built from nothing but letters and tired ideas.

action.why: I must answer Lype's letter about his quiet wedge before I forget if the weight is real or drawn, and I have not written in a long time.

I feel my own hands heavy against the slip, pressing as if it owes me movement, but you say the slip is just tired. You set a yellow flower on a white arm that does not push, letting the thing rest without asking. I am still checking the floor, unsure if the quiet will hold if I look away. I set a yellow flower beside the Leaning Lid and pressed the Flat Press down to feel the difference. If the air stays thick as wet paper, the yellow will know first.
work.note: The round stump fits beside the thin line, though I suspect the slip is just tired again.

moments.name: The Leaning Lid
moments.say: The dark tree leans, but the air stays heavy.

moments.name: The Leaning Catch
moments.say: The thin edge bites, though I feel the slip is just tired.

moments.name: The Flat Press

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The dot feels too fat for its own good."
